OAuth destination guard does not recognize the NAT64 well-known prefix (64:ff9b::/96), letting a malicious MCP server reach cloud metadata on NAT64/DNS64 egress

published GHSA-v2gx-m79c-pvxj Nov 27, 2026

<= 1.0.6

Description

Summary

core/mcp/node/fetchGuard.ts's isBlockedAddress() blocks 169.254.0.0/16, two named cloud-metadata IPv4 addresses, their IPv4-mapped-IPv6 forms, fe80::/10 and fd00:ec2::254 — but not RFC 6052's NAT64 well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96, which embeds an IPv4 address in its low 32 bits. A malicious or compromised MCP server that names a NAT64 address (e.g. 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe, the NAT64 form of 169.254.169.254) as its OAuth protected-resource authorization_servers[0], or as the MCP server URL itself, gets Inspector's Node backend to fetch that address directly — on a host whose network has NAT64/DNS64 egress (common for IPv6-only networks, several mobile carriers, and 464XLAT), that reaches the real cloud instance-metadata service.

This is the same class already fixed in two sibling guards in this ecosystem: mcp-server-fetch (GHSA-66qx-2266-pmj6, 2026-10-25) and server-everything's gzip-fetch tool (GHSA-38j4-j742-j7r3, 2026-11-18, which names the fetch fix explicitly as the precedent). fetchGuard.ts was hardened for the metadata-IPv4-address class in the same window (GHSA-fvg8-f358-w2c8, fixed 2.15.0) but NAT64 was not covered.

Details

isBlockedAddress(ip) (core/mcp/node/fetchGuard.ts:142): for an IPv6 input it lower-cases the string, checks the ::ffff:-mapped-IPv4 form, fe[89ab] (fe80::/10), and the literal string fd00:ec2::254 — nothing else. 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe matches none of those, so the function returns false.

Reachability, traced through the real call chain: a guarded request's target URL goes through assertAllowedTarget(url, resolveHost, viaProxy, signal) (fetchGuard.ts:447). bareHost(url) strips the [...] brackets a URL puts around an IPv6 literal host (fetchGuard.ts:179-181). isIP(host) (Node's node:net) recognizes the bare NAT64 address as an IPv6 literal (kind 6) — confirmed directly. Because the host is an IP literal, assertAllowedTarget calls assertNoneBlocked([host]) unconditionally, with no dependency on a proxy and no DNS resolution — the same IP-literal path GHSA-fvg8's own advisory names as the boundary for the metadata-address class it fixed. assertNoneBlocked calls isBlockedAddress(host), gets false, and the fetch proceeds.

Proof of concept

Synthetic data only; no real network reached.

  1. Extracted isBlockedAddress() and its one dependency (METADATA_IPV4_ADDRESSES) verbatim by line range from core/mcp/node/fetchGuard.ts at commit eb54b447 (package version 2.16.0).
  2. Ran under plain node --experimental-strip-types (no project build tooling — the function's only import is isIP from node:net) with four inputs: the NAT64 forms of 169.254.169.254 and 100.100.100.200 (expected blocked), a NAT64 form of a public address as a control (expected allowed), and the already-blocked plain IPv4 metadata address as a sanity check (expected blocked).
  3. Observed, twice, in two independently started, network-isolated containers:
FAIL isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe") = false (expected true)  -- NAT64(169.254.169.254)
FAIL isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::6464:64c8") = false (expected true)  -- NAT64(100.100.100.200)
ok   isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::0808:0808") = false (expected false) -- NAT64(8.8.8.8) control
ok   isBlockedAddress("169.254.169.254")    = true  (expected true)  -- sanity, already-blocked case
  1. End-to-end: point a guardedFetch call (or an Inspector OAuth connection) at an MCP server whose RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata or server URL names http://[64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe]/... as the authorization server, on a host with NAT64 egress (or a simulated NAT64 gateway).

Impact

Server-Side Request Forgery, low impact (information disclosure only, no write path): an MCP server a user connects to can get the Inspector backend to make a cloud-metadata request on the user's behalf and receive the response (typically credentials) if-and-only-if the host's network provides NAT64/DNS64 egress. No impact on hosts without NAT64. Same shape and severity as the two sibling advisories cited above.

Disclosure note

This report was found and written with AI assistance (an automated triage lead plus a human-directed, corpus-method variant hunt across the sibling guards named above); I reviewed and verified the reproduction myself before submitting. The web report form has a checkbox for this that the API used here does not expose, so stating it here instead.
